test_title: PYST 20 - SSC CHSL 2025 - English Language (Held On: 19 Nov, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: english
question:
**Choose the correct passive voice transformation of the sentence:**

The new CEO has promised to give all employees a substantial bonus at the end of the year.

options.text: All employees have been promised a substantial bonus at the end of the year by the new CEO.
A substantial bonus have been promised to all employees by the new CEO at the end of the year.
All employees will be given a substantial bonus at the end of the year by the new CEO.
A substantial bonus will be promised to all employees by the new CEO at the end of the year.

solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Tense Identification:** The original sentence "has promised" is in the **Present Perfect** tense.
 
• **Passive Voice Rule:** To convert Present Perfect to Passive, the structure is "**has/have + been + past participle (V3)**".
 
• **Indirect Object as Subject:** This sentence has two objects: "all employees" (indirect) and "a substantial bonus" (direct). In Option 1, the indirect object "All employees" is correctly used as the new subject.
 
• **Subject-Verb Agreement:** Because "All employees" is plural, the auxiliary verb must be "**have**" (not "has").
 
• **Maintaining Meaning:** Option 1 preserves the exact tense and meaning of the original active sentence while shifting the focus to the employees.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"All employees have been promised a substantial bonus at the end of the year by the new CEO."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 2:** "A substantial bonus have been promised..." is grammatically incorrect because "a substantial bonus" is singular and requires "has," not "have."
 
• **Option 3:** "will be given" changes the tense from Present Perfect to Future Simple, altering the original meaning.
 
• **Option 4:** "will be promised" also incorrectly changes the tense to Future Simple.
